Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 7:47: Behold, you have learned that whenever the Holy One, blessed be He, grants greatness to the righteous, they lower themselves. Therefore Israel is compared to a vine, as it is said (Psalms 80:9), "You brought a vine out of Egypt" — just as with this vine, every cluster that is larger than another hangs lower than the other, so with Israel, whoever is greater must be more humble than his fellow (Yalkut, Part 1, §146). Similarly, an ordinary person bows in prayer four times — at the beginning and end of the first blessing [Avot] and at the beginning and end of Hoda'ah [thanksgiving] — but the High Priest bows at every single blessing, and the king bows at the beginning of every blessing and at its end (Berachot 34a-b), to teach you that the greater one is than his fellow, the more humble he must be.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 7:48: And when a person makes himself small, the Holy One, blessed be He, raises him up, as it is said (1 Samuel 2:8), "He raises the poor from the dust" etc. "and He causes them to inherit a throne of glory." Thus far from the book Menorat HaMaor of Rabbi Yisrael, peace be upon him, although I have abbreviated his words in some places, etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 7:49: Likewise we find several Tannaim and Amoraim in the Gemara who were praised for humility. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, in Bava Metzia (84b), said of Rabbi Elazar, whom Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel esteemed as highly as his own son Rabbi — Rabbi's mind was troubled by this; he came and said to him, my son, let it not trouble you — he is a lion, son of a lion, while you are a lion, son of a fox. And it says further there (85a): rather, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel was humble.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 7:50: And further, we find several instances in the Gemara where sages were praised for the attribute of humility. Hillel the Elder — well known is what they said of him in tractate Shabbat (30b). And likewise Rabbi Perida in Eruvin (54b), who repeated the halakhah to his student four hundred times and did not become exacting [angry]. Bava ben Buta, in Nedarim, chapter Rabbi Eliezer (66b); see there. And further in Sotah, chapter "Elu Ne'emarin" (40a): Rabbi Abahu said, at first I used to say, "I am humble" etc.; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 7:51: With this the chapter concludes, and this gate concludes:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 7:52: Blessed be the LORD forever, Amen and Amen.
